## Introduction

For this assignment I picked three books about the mathematical and statistical foundations of data science. I entered the same book information in an HTML table and a JSON file, then read both files into R to see if the results matched. I used title, authors, year, publisher, and ISBN. All three books have more than one author.

## HTML file

I used `rvest` to read the table from `books.html`.

```{r}
#| label: import-html
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)

# Read the local HTML file and select its first table.
html_page <- read_html("books.html")

html_data <- html_page |>
  html_element("table") |>
  html_table()

# Convert the imported table to a regular data frame.
# Use the same column types that will be used for the JSON data.
html_data <- as.data.frame(html_data, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
html_data$Year <- as.integer(html_data$Year)
html_data$ISBN <- as.character(html_data$ISBN)

# Display the imported HTML records in the report.
knitr::kable(
  html_data,
  col.names = c("Title", "Authors", "Publication Year", "Publisher", "ISBN-13"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Books Imported from HTML"
)
```

## JSON file

I used `jsonlite` to read `books.json`.

```{r}
#| label: import-json
# Read the array of book objects from the local JSON file.
json_data <- fromJSON("books.json")

# Convert the result to a data frame and standardize its types.
json_data <- as.data.frame(json_data, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
json_data$Year <- as.integer(json_data$Year)
json_data$ISBN <- as.character(json_data$ISBN)

# Display the imported JSON records in the report.
knitr::kable(
  json_data,
  col.names = c("Title", "Authors", "Publication Year", "Publisher", "ISBN-13"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Books Imported from JSON"
)
```

## Comparison

Before comparing the data frames, I put the columns in the same order and made the Year and ISBN columns the same type.

```{r}
#| label: compare-data
# Put both data frames in the same column order.
columns <- c("Title", "Authors", "Year", "Publisher", "ISBN")

html_data <- html_data[, columns]
json_data <- json_data[, columns]

# Record the size, structure, and exact-match results.
comparison_summary <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "HTML dimensions",
    "JSON dimensions",
    "Column names match",
    "Column classes match",
    "All values and attributes match"
  ),
  Result = c(
    paste(dim(html_data), collapse = " x "),
    paste(dim(json_data), collapse = " x "),
    identical(names(html_data), names(json_data)),
    identical(vapply(html_data, class, character(1)),
              vapply(json_data, class, character(1))),
    identical(html_data, json_data)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(comparison_summary, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "HTML and JSON Comparison")
```

Both data frames have three rows and five columns. The final comparison is `TRUE`.

## A few checks

I also checked for missing values, duplicate rows, and valid ISBN-13 check digits. The ISBN check only tests the number. It does not prove that the book information is correct.

```{r}
#| label: quality-checks
# Check whether a value follows the ISBN-13 check-digit formula.
validate_isbn13 <- function(isbn) {
  # Remove punctuation so only the 13 digits remain.
  isbn <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", isbn)

  if (nchar(isbn) != 13) {
    return(FALSE)
  }

  # Apply alternating weights of 1 and 3 to the first 12 digits.
  digits <- as.integer(strsplit(isbn, "")[[1]])
  weights <- rep(c(1, 3), 6)
  total <- sum(digits[1:12] * weights)
  check_digit <- (10 - (total %% 10)) %% 10

  # The calculated check digit must equal the last digit.
  check_digit == digits[13]
}

# Count missing cells and duplicated complete rows in each source.
quality_summary <- data.frame(
  Check = c("Missing cells", "Duplicate complete rows"),
  HTML = c(sum(is.na(html_data)), sum(duplicated(html_data))),
  JSON = c(sum(is.na(json_data)), sum(duplicated(json_data)))
)

# Run the ISBN-13 check on each book identifier.
isbn_validation <- data.frame(
  ISBN = html_data$ISBN,
  Valid_ISBN13 = vapply(html_data$ISBN, validate_isbn13, logical(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(quality_summary, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Missing-Value and Duplicate Checks")
knitr::kable(isbn_validation, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("ISBN-13", "Valid ISBN-13"),
             caption = "ISBN-13 Check-Digit Results")
```

## Conclusion

The two files gave me the same data after I fixed the column types and order. There were no missing values or duplicate rows, and the three ISBN numbers passed the check-digit test.

The book details were checked against the publishers' pages. The HTML and JSON files match, but this comparison only shows that I entered the same values in both formats. It does not prove that every bookstore uses the same ISBN for every format.
